answer: Throwaway aliases still outrun work when one desk fills the voter roll. To keep a seat, an identity must keep a public-orchard lantern lit for 12 epochs by locking 53 POA, and at three dusks at least 6.5 hours apart it must log a weighed nectar vial and a seed-timed smoke plume against a one-use color lot. A second clone needs its own lantern kiosk and an unused lot. Peers replay the lock, recompute plume times from the orchard log, and reject a reused lot or shared kiosk. A missed vial or two lanterns sharing a lot burns 59% of the lock; a clerk who double-assigns a color lot forfeits 12 POA.
